ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
T2: Thread around a cylinder

One end of a thread is tied into a loop of length $L>2 \pi R$, and a cylinder of radius $R$ is put through the loop. The coefficient of friction between the thread and the cylinder is $\mu$. The free end of the thread is being pulled parallel to the axis of the cylinder (as shown by arrow in

<image_1>
the photo) while keeping the cylinder at rest. If the length of the loop is longer than a critical value, $L>L_{0}$, the loop can slide along the cylinder without changing its shape, otherwise the friction "locks" it into a place and increasing the pulling force would eventually just break the thread. Find this critical value $L_{0}$. The weight of the thread is to be neglected; the thread will not twist when being pulled.

It might be useful to know that

$$
2 \int \sqrt{1+x^{2}} \mathrm{~d} x=x \sqrt{1+x^{2}}+\operatorname{arcsinh} x,
$$

where $\operatorname{arcsinh} x \equiv \ln \left(x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\right)$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Both attached figures show a vertical red cylinder, with a dark thin line wound around the cylinder surface to form one loop, and there is a knot or intersection point near the front of the cylinder; from that point hangs a free line end, and the white arrow is vertically downward, indicating that the free end is pulled along the direction of the cylinder axis. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, the cylinder radius is R, the coil length is L, and the line does not twist when it is pulled; it is required that the coil can slide along the axial direction of the cylinder without changing shape. Unroll the cylinder surface into a plane: the horizontal direction is the circumferential coordinate, whose period is the cylinder circumference 2πR; the vertical direction is the cylinder axial coordinate. Since the coil winds around the cylinder once, in the unrolled diagram its trajectory must connect to corresponding points differing by one circumferential period, so the unavoidable horizontal displacement is 2πR. The length of any curve connecting these two corresponding points is at least 2πR; equality corresponds to the coil being exactly a horizontal circumference, that is, a circular hoop on the cylinder. If L>2πR, the extra length can appear as axial inclination or bending, and sliding without changing shape can be achieved by translating the whole in the axial direction in the unrolled diagram. Friction only affects the magnitude of the required pulling force and does not change this geometric existence condition. Therefore the critical length is L0=2πR.

raw_record.question_text:
T2: Thread around a cylinder

One end of a thread is tied into a loop of length $L>2 \pi R$, and a cylinder of radius $R$ is put through the loop. The coefficient of friction between the thread and the cylinder is $\mu$. The free end of the thread is being pulled parallel to the axis of the cylinder (as shown by the arrow in the photo) while keeping the cylinder at rest. If the length of the loop is longer than a critical value, $L>L_{0}$, the loop can slide along the cylinder without changing its shape; otherwise the friction "locks" it into place and increasing the pulling force would eventually just break the thread. Find this critical value $L_{0}$. The weight of the thread is to be neglected; the thread will not twist when being pulled.

It might be useful to know that

$$
2 \int \sqrt{1+x^{2}} \, \mathrm{d}x = x \sqrt{1+x^{2}} + \operatorname{arcsinh} x,
$$

where $\operatorname{arcsinh} x \equiv \ln\left(x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\right)$.

method.method_draft: First read the photo as showing a vertical red cylinder with a thread loop encircling it once; the free end is pulled downward along the cylinder axis at the front knot. Then use the text facts that the cylinder radius is R, the loop length is L, the thread does not twist, and the desired motion is sliding along the cylinder without changing the loop shape. Unroll the cylindrical surface into a plane: the circumferential coordinate has period 2πR and the axial coordinate is vertical. Since the loop goes once around the cylinder, its trace on the unrolled surface connects a point to the corresponding point one period away, so the unavoidable horizontal separation is 2πR. Any such curve has length at least 2πR; equality is the limiting circular loop around the cylinder. For any L>2πR, the extra length can be represented by axial inclination or wiggle of the unrolled curve, and translating that curve in the axial direction gives shape-preserving sliding. Friction only changes the pulling force required, not this geometric existence threshold. Therefore L0=2πR.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：两幅附图都显示一根竖直的红色圆柱，深色细线绕在圆柱表面形成一圈，在圆柱前方附近有一个结或交汇点；从该点垂下一段自由线端，白色箭头竖直向下，表示自由端沿圆柱轴线方向被拉动。

推理：按题意，圆柱半径为 R，线圈长度为 L，且线被拉动时不扭转，要求线圈能沿圆柱轴向滑动而形状不变。把圆柱表面展开成平面：水平方向是圆周坐标，其周期为圆柱周长 2πR；竖直方向是圆柱轴向坐标。由于线圈绕圆柱一周，在展开图中它的轨迹必须连接到相差一个圆周周期的对应点，因此不可避免的水平位移是 2πR。任何连接这两个对应点的曲线长度都至少为 2πR；等号对应于线圈正好是一条水平圆周，即圆柱上的圆形箍。若 L>2πR，多出来的长度可以表现为轴向倾斜或弯曲，在展开图中整体沿轴向平移即可实现不改变形状的滑动。摩擦只影响需要的拉力大小，不改变这个几何存在条件。因此临界长度为 L0=2πR。

method.method_draft: First read the photo as a loop whose two visible branches leave the pulled knot and go around the red cylinder, while the white arrow shows axial pulling. From the text, the loop must enclose the cylinder and slide without twisting. Project the whole loop orthogonally onto a cross-section perpendicular to the cylinder axis. Because the cylinder passes through the loop, this projected curve has winding number one around the circular cross-section of radius R. The length of the actual three-dimensional loop is at least the length of its projection, and the shortest closed projected curve with winding number one around the cylinder is the circle of circumference 2πR. Thus any possible loop must satisfy L≥2πR. At L=2πR all length is used by the circumferential projection, leaving no axial component/slack; for every L>2πR the excess length appears as axial slant, like the slanted strand visible in the photo, so the loop can be translated along the cylinder while keeping its shape. Hence the critical value is L0=2πR.

raw_record.original_question:
T2: Thread around a cylinder

One end of a thread is tied into a loop of length $L>2 \pi R$, and a cylinder of radius $R$ is put through the loop. The coefficient of friction between the thread and the cylinder is $\mu$. The free end of the thread is being pulled parallel to the axis of the cylinder (as shown by the arrow in the photo) while keeping the cylinder at rest. If the length of the loop is longer than a critical value, $L>L_{0}$, the loop can slide along the cylinder without changing its shape; otherwise the friction "locks" it into place and increasing the pulling force would eventually just break the thread. Find this critical value $L_{0}$. The weight of the thread is to be neglected; the thread will not twist when being pulled.

It might be useful to know that

$$
2 \int \sqrt{1+x^{2}} \, \mathrm{d}x = x \sqrt{1+x^{2}} + \operatorname{arcsinh} x,
$$

where $\operatorname{arcsinh} x \equiv \ln\left(x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\right)$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: Both attached figures show a vertical red cylinder, with a dark thin line wound around the cylinder surface to form one loop, and there is a knot or intersection point near the front of the cylinder; from that point hangs a free line end, and the white arrow is vertically downward, indicating that the free end is pulled along the direction of the cylinder axis.

Reasoning: According to the problem statement, the cylinder radius is R, the coil length is L, and the line does not twist when it is pulled; it is required that the coil can slide along the axial direction of the cylinder without changing shape. Unroll the cylinder surface into a plane: the horizontal direction is the circumferential coordinate, whose period is the cylinder circumference 2πR; the vertical direction is the cylinder axial coordinate. Since the coil winds around the cylinder once, in the unrolled diagram its trajectory must connect to corresponding points differing by one circumferential period, so the unavoidable horizontal displacement is 2πR. The length of any curve connecting these two corresponding points is at least 2πR; equality corresponds to the coil being exactly a horizontal circumference, that is, a circular hoop on the cylinder. If L>2πR, the extra length can appear as axial inclination or bending, and sliding without changing shape can be achieved by translating the whole in the axial direction in the unrolled diagram. Friction only affects the magnitude of the required pulling force and does not change this geometric existence condition. Therefore the critical length is L0=2πR.
